text: The Halcyon Event. US Army Private August Rennick survives a munitions-depot explosion in New Mexico unharmed and levitates the wreckage off his unit. He is the first documented Graded. No cause has ever been confirmed.
Halcyon Event. 1950-53: Korea, the first war with Graded soldiers on both sides. McCarthy-era hearings accuse Graded of being Soviet "plants"; PSI Graded are blacklisted.
Scattered Kindlings worldwide. A Cold War arms race in Graded recruitment begins.

The Algerian War. France deploys Graded paratroopers, and PSI interrogators are used in the Battle of Algiers (1957), part of the torture scandal that haunts France for decades. Algerian Graded fight for independence; many families who came to France afterward carry that history.
Aurelian Pharmaceuticals buys Rennick's blood samples from the Army and isolates Ichor, a synthetic catalyst. This stays secret.
Aurelian isolates Ichor (secret). 1962: Enhanced Persons Act; the Bureau is founded; registration on paper "Bureau papers" (no Grade Cards or colored bands yet; the letter ranks are internal only).
The DGPA is founded.
Independence. The British colonial "Native Enhanced Register," which conscripted Graded into colonial police and mines, is abolished; the NEPC follows in 1963.
The Enhanced Persons Act makes registration mandatory and creates the Federal Bureau of Enhanced Affairs.
Graded civil rights marches run alongside the wider civil rights movement, often uneasily. Some states pass "Special Persons" segregation laws, struck down in 1967.

The Nigerian Civil War. Both the federal army and Biafra field Graded units. Biafra's few Graded are famous for running supplies through the blockade (SPA couriers) and for the healers who worked themselves to death in the famine. The war's Graded veterans go unacknowledged for decades.
The Apollo 11 Moon landing; the Soviets publicly fly a COR cosmonaut the same year.
The first Graded Pride march in Port Harlan, broken up by police with fire hoses and dogs.

a declining port and steel town. Aurelian's 1972 move brings money to downtown, which is still called the "Exchange District" (renamed the Spire after 1994). Riverside has union docks and the mob. The Old Foundry is still a working-class steel neighborhood, mostly baseline. Kesler Heights is new postwar suburbs.
The oil boom. Oil companies hire Graded for pipelines, rigs, and security. Lagos explodes in size. Afrobeat-era nightlife features Graded performers.
The Saigon Burn. A US-deployed S-Rank Flares during an operation and kills about 40,000 people. 1974: the Halden Accords restrict the military use of S-Ranks.
The Saigon Burn. An S-Rank Flare kills about 40,000 in Vietnam. The antiwar movement explodes.
Aurelian moves its headquarters to Port Harlan. Watergate burglary (a TEC Graded wiretapper is among those arrested).

Oil crisis. Graded "Heat Sinks" (KIN fire and electric users) are hired to run struggling power stations. The Ferris Hit: an NFL linebacker with an unregistered COR power kills an opponent on live TV.
Halden Accords signed. Nixon resigns. The Enhanced Evidence Act (1975) bars PSI testimony from court after the Watergate hearings.
Bicentennial. All major pro sports ban Graded athletes.
The Blackout of '77. A KIN Flare at a Manhattan substation leads to a citywide blackout, then riots aimed at Graded.
The Grade Card Act. Color-banded Grade Cards become mandatory.
Three Mile Island (a Heat Sink worker is credited with preventing worse). The Iran hostage crisis begins. The Old Foundry steel mills begin closing.
Operation Eagle Claw. The hostage rescue fails when the SPA teleporter on the mission Flares. Reagan wins.

the mills close (1979-83). Graded families, priced and pushed out of everywhere else, move into the Foundry's empty tenements. Crack and Burn arrive; Pinnacle billboards go up downtown; Ashgrove grows rich.
Hostages released. Mandatory school Kindle-marker screening (ages 12, 15, 18) begins.
Le secret du rang becomes law.
The Psi Panic. Daycare "mind control" accusations lead to trials and lynchings of PSI Graded; nearly all the accusations are later proven false.
Aurelian licenses the first corporate hero team, the Pinnacle.
Aurelian licenses the Pinnacle, the first corporate hero team. The Grenada invasion is its first "assist."
The LA Olympics formally ban Graded athletes. The rival Enhanced Games launch in Las Vegas.
Chernobyl. Soviet Graded Liquidators die containing the reactor; one survivor becomes the SS-Rank "Graphite." The Sump opens.
Black Monday. The market crash is blamed on a CAU trader, the "Wall Street Jinx," and CAU Graded are banned from trading floors. Halcyon is sighted in public for the last time, at age 62.
Drought. Weatherman (SS) breaks it on live TV and becomes a national hero.
The Berlin Wall falls after the Stasi's Graded unit refuses orders.
The Gulf War, the first televised Graded war. Aurelian Defense heroes fight alongside US forces. Paragon, the Pinnacle's founding leader, is killed in Kuwait; the nation mourns.
after Paragon's death, Tidewater leads; new members cycle through faster as the Pinnacle becomes a TV product. Bulwark joins in 1998.

the Foundry Riots (1992). Aurelian Tower is built (1994). The Exchange District becomes "the Spire," and gentrification starts pushing poorer residents toward Riverside. Kesler Heights booms with white-flight and baseline-flight families. The Choir starts as a small Riverside crew.

when the USSR collapsed, thousands of Graded were left unpaid and armed. They became bodyguards, enforcers, and Bratva "brothers," and the Loose Graded crisis gave Moscow's '90s their reputation. Graded oligarch bodyguards are still a status symbol.
The USSR collapses, and its ~4,000 Graded scatter: the "Loose Graded" crisis. Strategic Assets Act.
The Foundry Riots. Port Harlan police officers are acquitted after beating D-Rank courier Calvin Merritt on video; the Old Foundry burns for three days.
The Hollow Creek Siege. A 51-day standoff with a PSI cult leader in Texas ends in fire.
Aurelian Tower is completed. Newborn Kindle-marker screening begins. Granite becomes a Department of Defense asset.
The Ghostline Trial. A Pinnacle member is acquitted of murdering his ex-wife, and the verdict splits America along Graded and baseline lines.
The Tenant moves a mountain in Kazakhstan. The dot-com boom; TEC Graded command huge salaries.
Bulwark joins the Pinnacle.
The Chicago Flare. An S-Rank's uncontrolled release levels six city blocks and kills 2,300. Strain science goes mainstream. 2003: Quell, the first power suppressant, is approved.
The Chicago Flare kills 2,300. Y2K panic; TEC Graded are hired to fix code.
Return to civilian rule. Nollywood booms through the 2000s with Graded hero films on VHS and VCD.

2003, Quell is approved and policing changes overnight. 2006, Meridian debuts in the Pinnacle. 2008, the financial crash, and Halcyon falls into a coma. 2009, Lantern, Ohio is evacuated (Project Lantern). Tech: flip phones, then the iPhone (2007); MySpace and early YouTube clips of Graded fights; reality TV booms (Rookie Season, 2004).
The franc becomes the euro.
The banlieue riots. Augmented units patrol the cités; Graded youth form crews like the Sans-Rang.
Halcyon (Rennick) falls into an unexplained coma.

2011, the alleged Granite carrier incident. Also in 2011, the Low Kings form in Riverside. 2014, Rush hits the streets. 2015, Baseline Protection Act. 2017, Proxy escapes Russia; Flatline forms. 2019, the Hush Band Law. Tech: smartphones, social media, GradeWatch (2013), RankMatch (2015), viral hero clips. Hero brands live and die on Instagram.
Rush, a street drug made from stolen Ichor, appears.
Hush Band Law: PSI-category Graded of B-Rank and above must wear inhibitor bands in public.
Global pandemic. BIO healers are conscripted under emergency law; healers can't cure the virus at scale, and several die of exhaustion. Graded essential workers are hailed, then forgotten.
Riot in the Sump.
Flatline publicly kills the A-Rank hero Cascade.
The Halsey Street Incident (officially a "villain explosion"). Flatline kills Cascade on a livestream.
Flatline is designated a terrorist organization.
Equal Ground's Grade Card case is accepted by the Supreme Court. "Choirsong" Rush appears.
The present.
